clue.text: Argentine team's beef — bit near bone

blocks.note: argentine is an old word meaning silvery, from Latin argentum, silver
a team is a side; the 's joins the two words

explanation.surface: A grumble about a football team from Argentina, which then lurches into butchery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Argentine' looks like the country's adjective, but here it is the metal-coloured sense. Silverside is a British cut of beef from the outer thigh of the hindquarter.
explanation.definitionFit: Silverside is a joint of beef cut from the rump end of the leg, beside the thigh bone.

clue.text: Extreme elements in Supreme Court forming splinter group

indicators.note: the extreme elements of words are their outermost letters, first and last

blocks.note: first and last letters of Supreme
first and last letters of Court

explanation.surface: Extremists on a supreme court break away to form their own faction.
explanation.definitionFit: A sect is a small group that has broken away from a larger religious or political body.

clue.text: Indigenous person left something useful on phone

blocks.note: L is the standard abbreviation for left
an app is a handy program on a smartphone

explanation.surface: Someone forgot a useful item on their phone, or left their phone somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lapps, now usually called Sami, are the native people of northern Scandinavia.

clue.text: Improperly earn interest as company, perhaps

indicators.note: doing something improperly means not in the right way, so the letters fall out of their right order

blocks.note: the fodder, twelve letters

explanation.surface: A company that makes money from interest in an underhand way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Company' wants to be a business, which suits the money surface; here it is a theatrical company, and 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A company of actors is one example of a group of performers who amuse audiences.

clue.text: Aggressive outburst in nasal voice

indicators.note: in says the wanted word lies inside the next words, spanning across them

blocks.note: found running across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Someone launches into an angry tirade in a whiny, nasal tone.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a burst of gunfire, and figuratively a vigorous verbal attack.

clue.text: Part of navy does, for example, around second besieged city

indicators.note: around says the first item wraps itself about what follows

blocks.note: does are female deer, so they are an example of deer
S is the abbreviation for second
Troy was besieged by the Greeks for ten years

explanation.surface: A naval unit does its part around a second city under siege.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does' reads as a verb but is the plural of doe.
explanation.definitionFit: A destroyer is a fast warship, one of the vessels making up a navy's fleet.

clue.text: City with famous listed building

blocks.note: surface reading: a building protected by heritage listing
setter's reading: listing means leaning to one side, so this is a city whose famous building tilts

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a listed building is one protected for its historic value; a ship that lists leans over, which points to a famous tilting tower.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian city is famous for its tower that leans noticeably to one side.

clue.text: With minimal subscription, one name above all covered by that article I edited

indicators.note: something covered by others has them wrapped round it, so these words go inside
in a down entry, above means placed before what follows

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
N is the abbreviation for name
it is the pronoun standing for that article, a thing
taken as written
taken as written
ED is the abbreviation for edited

explanation.surface: Someone signs with just their initials, a single name set above everything in an edited article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' tempts you towards A or THE, but 'that article' is the pronoun for a thing; ALL is the part held inside, with I and N on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Subscribing a document means signing beneath it; doing so with only initials is the least possible signature.

clue.text: Leading to extreme upset, declare, having secured runs briskly added to score

indicators.note: having secured something means holding it fast inside
in a down entry, upset turns a word upside down, so it reads from bottom to top
leading to means one part comes first and runs into the next

blocks.note: to allege is to declare something to be so
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
OTT is over the top, extreme

explanation.surface: A cricket captain declares after a brisk run-scoring spell, which looks like an extreme upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' suggests a cricket total but is a musical score; 'runs' gives only the cricket abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegretto is an Italian tempo marking written on music, meaning fairly brisk.

clue.text: Economic system's statement that's valid for Mali or Morocco

blocks.note: the true statement begins 'capital is', speaking of an initial letter
both country names start with the same capital letter

explanation.surface: An economist states something true of two North-West African countries.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital means the initial capital letter, not the capital city that Mali or Morocco calls to mind; the 's on the definition reads as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Capitalism is the economic system built on private ownership and markets.

clue.text: Determination that could decide who succeeds

blocks.note: first meaning: resolve, strength of purpose
second meaning: the legal document naming who inherits

explanation.walkthrough: 'succeeds' looks like achieving success but means succeeding to property after a death.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both firm resolve and the legal testament directing who inherits an estate.

clue.text: Way old American serving in pub is obsessive

indicators.note: in places the serving soldier inside the word for the pub

blocks.note: a path is a way
O is the abbreviation for old
a local is one's neighbourhood pub, in British usage
a GI is a serving American soldier

explanation.surface: An old American who waits on tables in a pub is fixated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serving' suggests a bar worker but marks a soldier in service.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathological, used loosely, describes compulsive behaviour beyond reason, as in a pathological liar.

clue.text: Expert from university town checking manuscript

blocks.note: a pro is a professional, an expert
of can mean from, as in 'a man of Kent'
Reading is an English town with a university, west of London

explanation.surface: An expert from a university town goes through a manuscript.
explanation.definitionFit: Proofreading is the job of checking written copy for errors before it is printed.

clue.text: Horse that's not competitive for any course except the first

definitions.text: for any course except the first

blocks.note: first meaning: a horse entered for a race that fails to run, or has no chance

blocks.clueFragment: for any course except the first
blocks.note: second meaning: in a meal, every course after the starter is not the starter

explanation.walkthrough: 'course' slides from a racecourse to a course of a meal, and the first course of a meal is the starter.
explanation.definitionFit: The term means a horse with no chance of winning, and cryptically any meal course that is not the opening dish.

clue.text: One Northern European eclipsed by poet is amateur

indicators.note: something eclipsed is hidden behind another body, so these go inside the poet

blocks.note: Dante Alighieri, the Italian poet
I is the Roman numeral for one
a Lett is a Latvian

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian outshone by a great poet turns out to be a mere hobbyist.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilettante dabbles in an art or subject without professional commitment.

clue.text: As a rule, not many get involved in it

definitions.text: As a rule, not many get involved in it

blocks.clueFragment: As a rule, not many get involved in it
blocks.note: surface reading: generally few people take part in something
setter's reading: in the matter of ruling, only a few are involved, government by a small group

explanation.walkthrough: 'As a rule' looks like 'usually' but means 'as a system of rule'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is government by a small elite, so in this form of rule few people have a share.

clue.text: Dramatic victim of disaster in pectoral area

indicators.note: a disaster throws everything into ruin, so the letters are wrecked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, as fodder
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A victim in a stage play suffers a catastrophe in the chest area.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: in Shakespeare the asp bites at her breast.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra dies in Shakespeare's play Antony and Cleopatra, so she is a victim in a drama.

clue.text: Make a score of 40 or 50 in encounter

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the word for encounter

blocks.note: to have trouble is to encounter it
L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.surface: Reads like a sporting tally of 40 or 50 in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: A score is twenty, so cutting 40 in two makes a score.
explanation.definitionFit: Halving divides something into two equal parts, and half of forty is twenty, a score.

clue.text: Novelist that can hold a lot of beer

definitions.text: that can hold a lot of beer

blocks.note: first meaning: Gertrude ..., American writer

blocks.clueFragment: that can hold a lot of beer
blocks.note: second meaning: a large beer mug

explanation.definitionFit: The word is the surname of the writer Gertrude Stein and also a big earthenware tankard.

clue.text: Enter with four letters from Lima after botching registration

indicators.note: botching a job does it clumsily, so the letters are messed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
Lima is L in the radio alphabet; the four letters starting there

explanation.surface: Someone joins up with a few letters from Peru's capital after messing up the sign-up form.
explanation.walkthrough: Lima looks like Peru's capital but is the NATO code word for L, the start of an alphabet run.
explanation.definitionFit: Enrolment is the act of signing on officially, a registration on a list or course.

clue.text: Right work inserted in literary collection for man's study

indicators.note: inserted in places one part inside another

blocks.note: an anthology is a collection of writings
R is the abbreviation for right
OP is opus, a work

explanation.surface: The right piece is added to an anthology for someone's study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man's study' sounds like a room in a house but means the study of mankind.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthropology is the academic study of humankind and its societies.

clue.text: Authorized to follow pedestrian path?

blocks.note: first meaning: legitimate, above board, in slang
second meaning: read as two words, ..., to go on foot

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second sense needs the answer split into two words; leg it is British slang for walking or running off.
explanation.definitionFit: Legit is informal for legitimate, lawfully sanctioned, while leg it means travel on foot.

clue.text: Sound rule that's exemplarily right

definitions.note: a noun phrase: the thing proverbially right, from 'as right as rain'

indicators.note: sound tells us to take what the next word would be when spoken

blocks.note: a reign is a period of rule

explanation.surface: A sensible rule that is a perfect model of being correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning sensible but is the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'right as rain' makes rain the standard example of being perfectly all right.

clue.text: After change of heart, shut up like this

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word reads from bottom to top
a change of heart rearranges the middle letters, here the central pair swapping places

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who has changed their mind falls silent, just like that.
explanation.walkthrough: Reversed, the word gives TUHS; swapping its two middle letters turns it into THUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Thus means in this way, so it substitutes for like this.

clue.text: Colour that's fashionable, time after time

indicators.note: after places the second item behind the first in the answer

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
in means in fashion
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A shade that keeps coming back into fashion, time after time.
explanation.definitionFit: A tint is a shade or hue, a variety of colour.

clue.text: Transport players' trainer?

blocks.note: first meaning: a horse-drawn passenger vehicle of old
second meaning: read as two words, someone who coaches actors on the stage

explanation.walkthrough: 'players' are actors, not sportspeople, and the question mark warns the coach here is a tutor.
explanation.definitionFit: A stagecoach was a horse-drawn public vehicle; a stage coach would train performers.

clue.text: Kind of knot that sailors try to avoid

blocks.note: first meaning: the square knot used for ... sails
second meaning: a ridge of rock or coral near the surface

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a common square knot and a dangerous underwater ridge that ships steer clear of.

clue.text: Shared communication systems on which politicians often vote

blocks.note: first meaning: telephone lines shared by several subscribers
second meaning: official policies members are expected to follow

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both telephone circuits shared by several households and a political party's official stance.
